pages.title: The sender’s need
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Message A · simulated source
pages.subject: A quick reply
paragraphs: “Please send a quick reply so I can plan the next stage.” The sender explains that long silence makes scheduling difficult. They want to know whether the request has arrived and when an answer can be expected. The message does not explicitly say whether quick means a receipt acknowledgement or a complete verified response.

Their underlying need is predictability. A useful reformulation should preserve that without turning it into a demand for unverified figures. The learner should check the intended meaning before assigning an unreasonable position to the sender. The fact that a request feels urgent does not establish that every part of it must be completed immediately.

pages.title: The receiver’s concern
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Message B · simulated source
pages.subject: Time to verify
paragraphs: “Verification of the requested figures requires additional time. We cannot give a reliable final answer today.” The receiver is concerned that a quick reply will be treated as a completed check. They want enough time to verify the figures before anyone acts on them. They have not rejected sending a receipt acknowledgement or a realistic estimate.

The dense wording is not inherently incorrect, but it leaves the person and next action less visible. A clearer oral version might say who is checking and when they will respond. The task is to identify the common ground, separate acknowledgement from completion and test a concrete example with both sides before declaring the disagreement resolved.

pages.title: Check the disputed word
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: When you say we need a quick reply, do you mean a full answer today?
lines.audioText: When you say we need a quick reply, do you mean a full answer today?
lines.translation: Quando diz que precisamos de resposta rápida, quer dizer uma resposta completa hoje?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Not necessarily. I need to know the request has been received and when a checked answer will follow
lines.audioText: Not necessarily. I need to know the request has been received and when a checked answer will follow.
lines.translation: Não necessariamente. Preciso saber que o pedido foi recebido e quando virá uma resposta verificada

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I’d taken quick to mean answering before checking the figures
lines.audioText: I’d taken quick to mean answering before checking the figures.
lines.translation: Eu tinha entendido rápido como responder antes de conferir os números

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That would be risky. What I mean is quick acknowledgement, not instant certainty
lines.audioText: That would be risky. What I mean is quick acknowledgement, not instant certainty.
lines.translation: Isso seria arriscado. Quero dizer confirmação rápida de recebimento, não certeza instantânea

questions.prompt: What did the listener initially infer?
questions.answer: A full answer before checking the figures

pages.title: An example makes the meaning testable
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So, if I understand you correctly, verification can still take until tomorrow?
lines.audioText: So, if I understand you correctly, verification can still take until tomorrow?
lines.translation: Então, se entendi corretamente, a verificação ainda pode levar até amanhã?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, provided the sender gives a realistic time and updates us if it changes
lines.audioText: Yes, provided the sender gives a realistic time and updates us if it changes.
lines.translation: Sim, desde que a pessoa dê um horário realista e avise se mudar

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: To put it another way, a message can be fast without pretending the answer is complete
lines.audioText: To put it another way, a message can be fast without pretending the answer is complete.
lines.translation: Em outras palavras, a mensagem pode ser rápida sem fingir que a resposta está completa

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. A concrete example would be: “Received. I’ll check the figures and reply by four tomorrow.”
lines.audioText: Exactly. A concrete example would be: “Received. I’ll check the figures and reply by four tomorrow.”
lines.translation: Exatamente. Um exemplo concreto seria: “Recebido. Vou conferir os números e responder até as quatro de amanhã.”

questions.prompt: What does the concrete example add?
questions.answer: Who will check and when the answer will follow

pages.title: Find common ground without assuming agreement
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: That also makes the next step easier to track than “verification of availability is ongoing”
lines.audioText: That also makes the next step easier to track than “verification of availability is ongoing”.
lines.translation: Isso também facilita acompanhar o próximo passo, mais do que “a verificação da disponibilidade está em andamento”

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes. The noun phrase isn’t wrong, but it can hide who is doing what and when
lines.audioText: Yes. The noun phrase isn’t wrong, but it can hide who is doing what and when.
lines.translation: Sim. A expressão nominal não está errada, mas pode esconder quem faz o quê e quando

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then our common ground is an accurate answer with a visible response time
lines.audioText: Then our common ground is an accurate answer with a visible response time.
lines.translation: Então nosso ponto em comum é uma resposta correta com prazo visível

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: And we should check that interpretation with the other person instead of announcing the disagreement is solved
lines.audioText: And we should check that interpretation with the other person instead of announcing the disagreement is solved.
lines.translation: E devemos conferir essa interpretação com a outra pessoa em vez de anunciar que a discordância acabou

pages.title: Quick acknowledgement, not unchecked certainty
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I think my request for a quick reply has been misunderstood. I wasn’t asking for the checked figures today. I was asking for a prompt acknowledgement and a realistic time for the complete answer. If verification takes until four tomorrow, please say that. What’s difficult is silence, followed by a rushed answer that looks final but hasn’t been checked. Could you explain both positions again so they can see the common ground? One person is protecting accuracy; the other is trying to plan around a response. A useful reformulation should make those needs visible and give an example, rather than repeat the word quick more loudly. Please check that they agree with your summary before treating it as their settled position
